Hi Audrey — answering your two items with specifics so you can map into SIG/CAIQ sections: 

Ephemeral wrapping narrative (summary):
- Wrap keys: a fleet-level Key Encryption Key (KEK) pair is provisioned and stored in our FIPS-140-2/3 validated HSM cluster. KEKs are hardware-protected and never exported in plaintext.
- Tenant ephemeral keys are generated in-memory on the serving node and immediately encrypted (wrapped) under the active KEK before any persistent storage. The unwrapped key material resides only in ephemeral process memory and KV caches with strict TTLs.
- Rotation: KEKs are rotated quarterly by default; an emergency rewrap flow exists that performs a rolling re-encrypt (re-wrap) of persisted wrapped keys under a new KEK with atomic handoff and verification steps logged.
- Access control: KEK wrap/unwrap operations are restricted to HSM operator roles and a limited daemon identity. All wrap/unwrap attempts are audited and indexed for quick lookups.

Shift logs extract (what we'll provide):
- For PrismBank we will provide: shift start/end times, operator redaction tokens (OP-001 style), action categories (e.g., BACKUP, UNWRAP, SEAL, AUDIT), and a SHA256 checksum for each daily log file.
- We will not include command-level payloads or any private key material.

Notes / validation items:
- We can adopt your preferred redaction token format if you provide an example.
- If you want additional fields (e.g., IP of operator console), say so now and we'll evaluate PII risk.

I'll attach the policy PDF and a small sample of redacted shift-log CSV for quick review.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Cryptography Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: ephemeral-wrap-policy-2026-07.pdf (PDF), sample-shiftlog-redacted.csv (CSV)
